author: Nancy Burns-Fusaro
title: Rodney Crowell, The Secret Sisters, to perform at the United
text:
WESTERLY — Rodney Crowell, a multi-Grammy Award-winning troubadour known as a "songwriter’s songwriter" and "an icon among giants," will bring his Airline Highway Tour to the United Saturday as part of "Nashville North."
Crowell, who has written 15 number one hits, came up in Nashville’s songwriting heyday alongside Guy Clark, Townes Van Zandt and Steve Earle and has continued that legacy of camaraderie and kinship with his peers well into the iconic era of his career, according to his website.
Over the course of his career, the native Texan has "gracefully blended his own mainstream success as an artist with a prolific catalog of songs cut by the likes of Emmylou Harris, Johnny Cash, Waylon Jennings and Keith Urban, making him a master among his peers," the website says.
With more than 40 years of American roots music under his belt, it continues, "Crowell has also been cited as the architect of Americana music, extending his genre reach, but owing to the distinctly universal, literary quality of his writing, he has also penned beloved songs for artists as diverse as Bob Seger, Etta James, the Grateful Dead, John Denver, Jimmy Buffett and countless others."
A member of the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, Crowell is also the author of the acclaimed memoir, "Chinaberry Sidewalks," and teamed up with New York Times best-selling author Mary Karr for "Kin: Songs by Mary Karr & Rodney Crowell" in 2012, with Karr saying of her collaborator, "Like Hank Williams or Townes Van Zandt or Miss Lucinda, he writes and croons with a poet’s economy and a well digger’s deep heart."
Crowell was honored with ASCAP’s Founder’s Award in 2017, and that same year released the album “Close Ties,” which spawned another Grammy nomination for “It Ain’t Over Yet” with Rosanne Cash and John Paul White in the category of Best Americana Song. “Texas” was a collection of Lone Star-centric collaborations with Ringo Starr, Willie Nelson, Ronnie Dunn, Steve Earle and more, and Crowell’s most recent album release is the 2021 set, “Triage.”
A duo called The Secret Sisters, featuring Laura Rogers and Lydia Slagle, a pair of "Alabama-bred siblings," will open for Crowell. The country-folk duo is touring behind their fifth album, “ Mind, Man, Medicine,” which they have said , "explores the complexities of motherhood, commitment, compassion, and self-preservation in an endlessly chaotic world."
"Nashville North," the much-heralded cultural exchange designed to bring country and Americana music from around the country to to Rhode Island while celebrating Nashville’s notable music scene and Westerly's
Tickets are $63.60 and $68.60 at unitedtheatre.org.
— Nancy Burns-Fusaro
